discharged_blockers.blocker: (1) WRITE-CONFIRM. A self-corpus pin arc contains a `create_file` step. A replay may only CONFIRM such a step when the exact bytes were approved by a human (`playbook_blobs` via `aios/core/replay_writes.py::load_content`). The self-corpus has no human, and registering agent-written bytes as approved would be forging an approval.
discharged_blockers.discharged_by: Not discharged -- ROUTED AROUND. A pin arc still cannot be replayed, and that guard is correct: registering agent-written bytes as human-approved would be forging an approval. The verify-only arc has no create_file step, so the guard never applies rather than being weakened. `playbook_blobs` and `replay_writes.load_content` are untouched.

discharged_blockers.blocker: (2) APPROVAL GATE. The write-free alternative -- a read+verify arc over a real module -- is blocked at the gateway: `pytest` is on the YELLOW (approval-required) list, and the auto-execute allowlist is `echo` and `pwd` only. An unattended training run has no approver, so the verify never executes. Observed directly: `tool_blocked` on `pytest tests/test_code_chunking.py` inside the corpus.
discharged_blockers.discharged_by: Operator granted the scoped approval on 2026-09-22 (asked for by name in this ledger's previous revision). The gateway is unchanged -- `pytest` stays YELLOW for everyone else, which tests/test_training_approval_is_narrow.py::TestTheGatewayItselfIsUnchanged fails if anyone reclassifies it. Approval still cannot buy RED (execute_approved re-evaluates) and the scope lock still confines the command to the throwaway worktree; both directions are asserted in that file.

Proposals also LEAVE the process now (.aios/audit/curriculum-proposals.jsonl, accepted=false) -- what used to leave was a log line counting them, so the authority boundary the miner protects had nothing on the other side of it to accept. tests/test_curriculum_mining_is_live.py carries the positive assertions AND the negative control that the toy world still mines the toy way.
